contexts.text: Lest thou be consumed () = if otherwise, it would perish.
That falsity from evil would consume. Signified.
It is the falsity of evil which consumes good; evil itself is opposed to good, but by itself does not consume goods, but through falsity...
The silver was consumed from the land of Egypt () = that the true scientific was no longer visible in the Natural and within the Church.
The bush was not at all consumed ()... Not to be consumed with fire = not to be dissipated by the good of Divine love.
Hence the Lord is so often called a consuming fire. AE 504:20.
Consumption in general. Signified. Here, the consumption of truth... The consumption of good. Signified.

The consumption of all things which have anything from truth. Signified. The truth not consumed by the former falsity. Signified. These are the falsities which consume the most general truths and goods.
He would be consumed in a moment... AC 8760:end. AC 8816.
The consumption of cohering goods. Signified.
By to desolate is here signified the consumption which is effected through cupidities, for these are fires which consume...
That consumption through cupidities is meant by this word in the Original Language. Illustrated.
To consume, when predicated of Jehovah, = to perish by their own evil. Explained. AC 10439. AC 10533.
It would consume all their life.
Fire came down from God out of Heaven, and consumed them () = that they perished by the concupiscences of infernal love.
The Angels would be consumed...
The dissipation of evils and falsities which are against the truths and goods of the Church, is signified by, thou shalt consume all the people which Jehovah thy God shall deliver thee ().
They shall consume, into smoke shall they consume away () = that they will perish through falsities of evil.
The cupidities of falsity which utterly consume. Signified.
The vintage shall be consumed () = that the truth of the Church shall be no more.
Thy posterity shall be consumed by the fire () = that the rest will perish through earthly loves.
To be consumed by the sword, or famine = to be destroyed through falsities and evils.
To consume the birds of the heavens, and the fishes of the sea () = to destroy spiritual and natural affection.
